There's still an issue if the length of an FT_UINT_STRING is longer than the packet. ptvcursor_add_ret_string() throws an exception and the user just sees a generic "Malformed Packet (Exception occurred)" expert info. How would you handle that, if at all?

> How would you handle that, if at all?

By letting `ptvcursor_add_ret_string()` throw an exception; that's how all of our dissectors handle a packet with a field that runs past the end of the packet.

There's not much more to say in the message, other than having the calls to add fields to the protocol tree record the field information somewhere available to the exception handler, and having the exception handler say "Malformed packet (field foo.bar runs past the end of the packet)" (or the equivalent message for running past the *captured* data if the packet was sliced)

> By letting `ptvcursor_add_ret_string()` throw an exception

Then I leave it as it is.

> having the exception handler say "Malformed packet (field foo.bar runs past the end of the packet)" (or the equivalent message for running past the *captured* data if the packet was sliced)

That would actually be a useful error message, even without the field name.

commits_data.title: D-Bus: Improve signature validation
commits_data.message:
D-Bus: Improve signature validation

An invalid signature ("a{sa}") caused a segfault when the array inside
the entry had a length of zero. An array signature code ("a") must be
followed by a single complete type, and "}" is not one of them. Check
additional restrictions for structs and dict entries, which aren't
related to this bug.

Fixes #17176
